vehicles.speed_basis: Normal top speed 40 km/h, from the Battlefield 4 infobox on the Battlefield Wiki M1 Abrams page ('40 KPH Standard; 56 KPH Max'). The 56 km/h boost figure was not used.
vehicles.note: Anchor tank, so ratio B is exactly 1.0, which sits on the slow/medium boundary (see unclear). I recorded medium. With the 56 km/h boost (15.56 m/s), A = 2.39 (still fast). The T-90 and Type 98 infoboxes give the same 40/56. The Comparison section says that after the 2015 Fall update the Abrams has the highest top speed of the three MBTs, so the infobox may predate that patch.

vehicles.speed_basis: Normal top speed 42 km/h, from the Battlefield 4 infobox on the Battlefield Wiki LAV-25 page ('42 km/h / 65 km/h (boost) / 28 km/h (in water)'). The boost figure was not used.
vehicles.note: With boost (65 km/h = 18.06 m/s), A = 2.78, which is very-fast. B = 1.63 (fast) against the Abrams' normal speed, or 1.16 (medium) boost against boost. The wiki says wheeled IFVs get a higher top speed than tracked MBTs. The ZBD-09 infobox matches (42/64).

vehicles.speed_basis: No Battlefield 4 figure exists: the English wiki's BF4 M1161 ITV infobox gives only 'man = Fast'. I used a proxy: 75 km/h, the Battlefield 3 Growler ITV top speed ('Höchstgeschwindigkeit') on the German Battlefield Wiki. The real-vehicle 105 km/h on the English page was not used.
vehicles.note: Judged, because the figure comes from the BF3 version. Both bands hold for any speed from 60 to 100 km/h (A 2.56-4.27, B 1.5-2.5). The BF4 Dirt Bike, which the wiki calls faster, is listed at 95 km/h. Against the boosted Abrams (56 km/h), B would be 1.34, which is medium.

vehicles.speed_basis: No Battlefield 4 figure on the wiki: the BF4 infobox has no speed field. I used a proxy: 330 km/h from the same page's Battlefield 3 infobox. The BF4 section says it behaves much like its BF3 version, and that it and the Mi-28 have a higher top speed than the Z-10W. Gamepressure's BF4 guide gives '160' (RU/US) against 130 (CH), in a game unit it says matches no real unit.
vehicles.note: The raw speed is uncertain, but the band is not. Even if Gamepressure's 160 is read as km/h (44.4 m/s), A = 6.8 and B = 4.0, both very-fast. B would only drop below very-fast under 100 km/h. Comparing an aircraft with a tank gives no extra information: every aircraft ends up very-fast either way.

vehicles.speed_basis: 66 km/h stock top speed on level ground, from the in-game speedometer as reported in the Steam 'Tank guide' (posted Feb 2018, updated Oct 2020): 'without upgrades is 66kph ... the fastest MBT'. With the Racer chassis it is 79 km/h (planetsideguide.com, seen only in a search snippet because the site is unreachable). The PS2 Wiki gives no figure; it only says the Prowler 'boasts a higher top speed' than the other tanks.
vehicles.note: Anchor tank, so B is exactly 1.0, on the slow/medium boundary; I recorded medium. The same guide gives the Vanguard 60 km/h and the Magrider 50 km/h, so with B the other MBTs would be slow (0.91, 0.76). The figure comes from a player guide that predates later patches. With Racer, A = 3.38.

vehicles.speed_basis: About 70 km/h on level ground, from the Steam 'Tank guide' (2018, updated 2020). A YouTube clip about the Rival Combat Chassis also shows 70 kph forward. The PS2 Wiki only says it is 'faster, more maneuverable and smaller' than the MBTs.
vehicles.note: Approximate figure ('about 70kph') from a player guide. B is just above 1.0, so it is medium under either boundary reading. Stock, no Racer chassis.

vehicles.speed_basis: 90 km/h stock top speed, from the Steam guide 'The Harasser' (posted May 2013, updated May 2025): 'top speed of 90KPH! (Unupgraded vehicle)'. Max Racer is 110 km/h. Turbo bursts were not used. NamuWiki (search snippet only) instead gives about 75-81 km/h with Racer.
vehicles.note: The sources conflict (90 stock vs 75-81 with Racer), and the 90 may predate the 2013 Harasser nerfs. A is very-fast throughout. B is medium for anything from 66 to 99 km/h; only the 110 km/h Racer speed against the stock Prowler (1.67) would make it fast, and 110 against a Racer Prowler (79) gives 1.39, still medium. The PS2 Wiki says only 'high speed', with a periodic turbo boost.

vehicles.speed_basis: No figure found on the PS2 Wiki, in Steam guides, on the forums or in the Census API. Judged from descriptions: the Steam 'Complete Sunderer Guide' (2014) calls it 'slow, and it's really freakin' huge' and says it loses speed in turns. Since the July 2024 rework it has no performance chassis. My estimate is about 55-65 km/h on the flat, a little below the Prowler.
vehicles.note: The estimate puts A at 2.35-2.78, right on the fast/very-fast line (58.5 km/h). I picked very-fast on a best guess of about 60 km/h (2.56); at 55 km/h it would be fast. B would be 0.83-0.98 (slow), on the assumption that it is not faster than the Prowler; at 66 km/h or more it would be medium.

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed 5.42 m/s (offspeed field in the infobox; also in the Movement Speed table), foxhole.wiki.gg. Road speed is 7.75 m/s. Diesel, no road-tier bonus.
vehicles.note: Anchor tank, so B is exactly 1.0, on the slow/medium boundary; I recorded medium. The figure itself is solid (wiki infobox). On road it would be A 1.55 (fast) and B 1.43.

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed 5.79 m/s (offspeed field in the infobox; also in the Movement Speed table), foxhole.wiki.gg. Road speed is 8.27 m/s.
vehicles.note: A light tank only 7% faster than the assault tank, so it is medium under both methods. On road: A 1.65 (fast), B 1.53 (fast).

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed 3.27 m/s (offspeed field in the infobox; also in the Movement Speed table), foxhole.wiki.gg. Road speed is 10.88 m/s. The page itself calls it 'mediocre off-road speed and decent on-road speed'.
vehicles.note: The off-road rule makes this wheeled armoured car slower than a walking soldier and than every tank. On road it is A 2.18 / B 2.01 (fast under both). The figures are solid; whether the band means anything is a rule question (see unclear).

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed 3.46 m/s at 0% encumbrance (infobox offspeed; the Movement Speed table gives 3.46 / 2.77 / 2.49 for 0% / 1-99% / 100%+ load), foxhole.wiki.gg. Road speed is 17.32 m/s empty.
vehicles.note: Used the empty-truck figure; any load lowers it further (2.77 gives A 0.55). On road it is the fastest of these four (A 3.46, B 3.20, very-fast). A logistics truck comes out very-slow only because of the off-road rule.

unclear: 1) Ratio exactly 1.0 is ambiguous. speed-bands.json says slow is '0.7 to 1' and medium is '1 to 1.5', so both bands include 1.0. Under method B every anchor tank (Abrams, Prowler, Silverhand) lands exactly on 1.0, so B needs a tie-break. I recorded medium. The fast band's wording ('over 1.5 and up to 2.5', i.e. lower bound excluded, upper included) would instead put 1.0 in slow, but the 0.7 boundary is worded the opposite way ('under 0.7' is very slow, so 0.7 is slow). The convention is not uniform. 2) Battlefield boost is unlimited. The Vehicle Boost page says BF3 removed the boost meter and BF4 works the same way. The soldier reference uses sprint precisely because sprint is unlimited, so using non-boost speeds for vehicles is inconsistent. Boost changes the LAV-25 under A (fast to very-fast) and the ITV under B (fast to medium, if the Abrams reference is boosted). 3) Method B for aircraft: dividing a helicopter by a tank puts every aircraft at 4-8x, so B separates nothing in the air. An air anchor, such as the game's transport helicopter, might be needed. 4) Foxhole's off-road rule makes wheeled vehicles (O'Brien 3.27, Dunne 3.46 m/s) very-slow under both methods: slower than a walking soldier and than any tank, even though on road they are the fastest units here. Also, Foxhole's soldier reference is walking (5 m/s) while Battlefield and PS2 use sprint (6.5), so method A is not comparable across games. 5) Method B compresses PlanetSide 2: Prowler, Lightning and Harasser all come out medium (1.0-1.36), and only the Sunderer moves (to slow). Under A, all PS2 vehicles are very-fast, so neither method separates them well. Thresholds of 1.5 and 2.5 may be too wide for vehicle-to-vehicle comparisons. 6) Which configuration counts as top speed: stock or upgraded (PS2 Racer chassis about +20%, Harasser turbo; Foxhole petrol +10% and road-tier bonuses; Foxhole encumbrance tiers). I used stock, diesel and empty everywhere. 7) Source quality: the BF4 ITV and AH-1Z have no BF4 figure, so I used BF3 values (75 km/h from the German wiki, 330 km/h from the English wiki), and Gamepressure gives the BF4 helicopter speed only in a non-real unit. All PS2 figures are player speedometer reports from 2013-2020 guides that predate later patches (the Harasser sources conflict: 90 stock vs 75-81 with Racer), and no Sunderer figure exists anywhere I could reach. Also, the Abrams wiki trivia says the 2015 Fall patch made the Abrams the fastest MBT, yet the infobox still lists the same 40/56 as the T-90 and Type 98, so the infobox may be pre-patch.
